To demonstrate the foolishness of those who still think the current American war against Iran makes sense solely under the concept of the "Islamic Republic" and not Iran as a whole, there is no shortage of evidence — from Rubio's recent remarks in Greece to this explicit interview by Trump with Michael Perchick, reporter for WTVD television network:

"Currently, they consider them the most evil country in the world. And it has been that way for a long time; for many, many years. You know, I've been hearing this for 47 years; [while] it's been five years... the truth is it seems like 52 years, but its history goes back even before that."

The historical instance of this view can also be found in history. In Book Five of the History of the Peloponnesian War, written by Thucydides, the dialogue between the Melians and the Athenians is detailed.

The story was that in 416 BC, Athens asked the small island of Melos to surrender to its empire. The Melians tried to maintain their neutrality and hoped that justice, independence, and the possibility of help from Sparta would protect them, but the Athenians stated their argument clearly:

"The issue is not only our present enemies; independent islands like you are also a danger to the empire, because they stand outside our order... if peoples maintain their independence, it is because they have power; and if we do not attack them, it is because we fear them. So by subjugating you, in addition to expanding our empire, we also increase our security; especially since you are islanders and weaker than others and should not be able to prevail over the masters of the sea."

(Thucydides, History of the Peloponnesian War, Book Five, Section 97)
